label: EXPERIMENTAL snowpack-structure prediction for expert decision support. Not an avalanche forecast, danger rating or operational guidance.
source: Avalanche Canada Mountain Information Network (public reports)

reports.title: Bow Summit
reports.comment:
quick: Wind gusting strong at ridgetop.
Skied N slopes with very light wind affect. / snowpack: Well settled snowpack to ground. 
CT easy RP down 25cm on DF, Hard BRK down 60 on MF crust
HS 90cm

reports.title: Bow Summit 171027
reports.comment: weather: Spring in October / snowpack: Not a very Rockies like snowpack. Strong bonding of recent storm snow. Evidence of basal faceting at ground and within the lower 10cms. Extreme warming and spring-like conditions by noon. Observed wind slab near ridge features. Fat snowpack in the deposit zones on NE to E aspects

reports.title: Bowcrow Peak avalanche
reports.comment: avalanche: Observed a sz 1.5-2 point release off a cliff on the steep NE  aspect of Bowcrow Peak from the highway. No step-down was seen upon hitting the mellower slopes at the bottom of the cliff

reports.title: 93 North Storm Slabs
reports.comment: avalanche: Triggered two small soft slabs today that failed on 5 to 10 cm of facets sitting above the Halloween Crust found down 30 to 50 cm. The first of these was pretty much the first turn below the truck on steep planar slope. The second was on a small moraine feature at 2500m.

reports.title: Bow Summit
reports.comment:
quick: Wind Slab, Specific lee to SW 1/2. Unreactive trending stubborn in PM. Possible Size 2. 
Soft Swd found to lack enough energy to crack/propagate, however became stiffer in PM.

reports.title: Avalanche Involvement - Crowfoot Moraines
reports.comment:
incident: Report came in from member of the public who was getting out of their car at the Crowfoot Glacier viewpoint. They heard a large avalanche and then heard screams for help. Banff Visitor Safety was called and mobilized a response, but was stood down enroute. 

Two skiers had been skinning up the fan below a couloir lookers left of the Crowfoot moraines when a large avalanche (likely loose …

reports.title: Helen Shoulder Glades
reports.comment: quick: First day out touring for the season. Went to treeline and completed a pit. 75 cm HS at treeline. ECT10/10@↓50 on facets.

reports.title: Cirque Peak Trees
reports.comment: quick: 5-10cm on top of rain/melt freeze crust up to 2300m. Mostly hard and wind affect above that. Crust was breakable and made for tricky skiing conditions, storm was intensifying around noon, moderate winds from the South.

reports.title: Upper Mosquito Creek
reports.comment: quick: Toured up the hiking trail to treed glades above the campground - good travelling conditions on solid melt/freeze base. 15-20 cm of fresh snow made for decent turns in the trees. Lot's of wind transport up high.

reports.title: Cirque Peak Trees South
reports.comment: quick: Up to 30cm new snow on top of rain crust. Conditions were much better than previous day, stayed out of the alpine and major avalanche paths. Low visibility most of the day, winds picking up at tree line around 1500h.

reports.title: Bow Summit 🤙
reports.comment:
quick: -6C at Bow Summit parking lot at 8am, -4 at 12.30pm. 

Ski quality was quite good at the tree runs south of the parking lot. 30cm of fresh snow over a supportive crust. No evidence of natural activity. Snow quality stayed consistent all day. 

Weather was light snow, moderate winds from the NW and broken skies.

reports.title: auto: Quick Report
reports.comment: quick: Pit at 2200m near tree line on sw aspect 33 degree slope 75cm deep, bottem 10cm was week facets with almost no desnity to it against the halloween crust lots of settle ments over the course of the day, produced a shear On the halloween crust putting the shovel behind the blok, did a propogation test, no results.. Mutiple crusts ( maybe a new one from sunday?) with right side up snowpack goi…

reports.title: Bow Peak
reports.comment:
quick: Wind ward aspects were pretty sparse, lots of rocks. Leeward sides had lots of snow.

Dug a pit on the NE aspect, in the alpine. It was 300 cm deep. We could definitely see a hard crust that was higher up in the column. We saw a fracture at CTH-6 about 80 cm down. 

We did not see any activity on the aspects we were on. There was probably 5-10 cm of new snow.

reports.title: Mt Jimmy Simpson
reports.comment:
snowpack: 11/30/2017 East aspect of Mt Jimmy Simpson. Winds calm, mostly cloudy -5°.
Snow pit at 2350m ENE aspect 30° slope. HS 145. SS 30. ECT NR-35. CTN-35. Halloween Crust very evident but not reactive, possibly due to low slope angle.
We were very surprised that we couldn't get any propagation on the Halloween layer or the November rain layer. Skiing was great, however.

reports.title: auto: Quick Report
reports.comment: quick: Snowing about 1-2cms all day with light to moderate winds from SSW.  -6c most of the day.  Obvious transport going on. The crust was there in some places but not in others.  Whiteout for a good portion of the day.

reports.title: Crowfoot Glades
reports.comment: quick: Epic day at Crowfoot glades. It was like a pow day at the resort. People skiing everywhere.  Stability was good, no signs movement. The snow was denser than usual, despite skiing thigh deep, so a steeper pitch was needed to link turns, which is why everyone came together. The upper alpine ridge was shedding the fresh snow late in the day when the wind picked up a little. It was a great day …

reports.title: Cirque Forepeak area
reports.comment:
quick: Good skiing today on the meadows below Cirque Forepeak. Approx 20cm of fresh-ish on the supportive late Nov crust. Saw a number of parties venturing into the alpine and getting what looked like thin turns. Ski out is in decent shape. 

It was -18 at 09.00, -6 at 14.30 and winds were light from the N/NW all day. Didn't see any significant transport occurring anywhere. Sky was clear with scat…

reports.title: bluebird
reports.comment: quick: Good skiing, stability seemed good, no signs of recent avalanche activity.  Did see lots of parties skiing with questionable terrain uses.  Lots of skiing straight up runouts (not necessary, ridges could have been utilized), transitioning mid runout, and skiers cutting across slope above.  Just a mini reminder to think about overhead hazard... be it from other skiers, cornice, etc.

reports.title: Crowfoot Mountain
reports.comment:
quick: Had a beautiful day today up at Crowfoot mountain. Light to moderate winds throughout the day. Temperatures were -21 at the Num-tih-jah lot at 8:30 a.m. and -7 when we returned at 3:15 p.m. Conditions through the gully were the best I have seen, easy travel. Watched a cornice drop/small size 1 loose dry avalanche from steep terrain over cliffs on a NW aspect. 

Windward slopes near the summ…

reports.title: Cirque N Glacier
reports.comment: quick: Good coverage on the Cirque N Glacier with 185cm of snow. One new natural windslab 15m x 30m x 30cms observed on a SE aspect at 2500m.  Winds were light in the morning then blowing steady in the moderate to strong range at noon from the north west at ridgetop. The glacier remained fairly sheltered and had limited wind effect at the end of the day with good skiing. The couloir off cirque pea…

reports.title: Mt Jimmy Simpson Junior
reports.comment: quick: We skinned up from the lodge parking lot through the trees and ascended Mt Jimmy Simpson Junior.  We gained the bench before the main slope and found a well consolidated 'right side up' snowpack.  About 10-15cm of dry low density snow that appears to have come without wind that increases in density until the ground where it was very firm.  Approximately 100cm HS.  We ascended the main slope…

reports.title: auto: Quick Report
reports.comment: quick: Parked at bow lake. Was -18 at the car at 7:30am, headed up the bow hut drainage in fantastic condition following a solid track til we started headed up towards crowfoot, dug a pit in the moraines on a Nw aspect at 2420m, 28 degrees 220cm deep, only dug down 125cm. No results on column test although 70cm deep above the november 23 crust there was a density change for 5cm at 70-75cm that was…

reports.title: Granddaddy couloir
reports.comment: quick: Went up to go and ski grand daddy couloir and found it to be full of very firm snow with some old debris.  It will need a cycle and then some snow until it is ready to be skied again.  We rode the fan beside it to salvage the day and had no signs if instability on assessment and the turns were good but not great, some wind crust, more than welcome experienced yesterday further north ok the …

reports.title: Wapta icefields conditions
reports.comment: quick: Stayed at bow hut from dec 9-13... Parking lot at 8am on sunday was 0. Arrived at the hut at 11:30am temp was -5 and extremly windy. Conditions on the icefields is very fast travel on hard wind packed sastruggi surface. Summited st nick skied the east face 20m below the peak to the hut, conditions were icy sastruggi and hard pack wind affect, slope was 45 degrees+ still very thin in spots. …

reports.title: Observation South Shouler
reports.comment: quick: South facing slopes, lightly gladed slopes at tree-line. Snowpack - Below the surface, the usually reported 50 cm of 'right-side up' snowpack above a supportive Nov crust. The surface - wind affected snow above tree-line, that made for variable skiing. Below tree-line was a 1 cm melt-freeze crust that softened to make spring skiing conditions at about 1400h under the sun. Skiing was good!

reports.title: Easy Laps at Bow Summit
reports.comment: quick: Rode easy laps all day all over the Bow Summit area. Ski conditions were very variable. Above and top of tree line was crusty or had hard wind slabs. Open slopes below tree line had large breakable crusts. Pieces varied from 1-3 inches thick and could be picked up solid in pieces up to 40cm. Found sections with heavy faceting. Ski penetration was only ever up to 5cm.  Surprisingly the best …

reports.title: Yoyo Turns in the East Bowl ofJimmy Simpson
reports.comment: quick: Went up into the bowl on the East side of Jimmy Simpson today. Ski quality was better than expected but in only in gully features and localized low spots. Enough flurries and  uphill and sideways wind transport has filled in these features and left a few 10cm deep powder turns for us to find amongst the hard slab. Some of these areas were firming up into a thin soft wind slab that was crack…

reports.title: Bow Summit study plot
reports.comment: quick: Weekly study plot profile. Notice the Dec 15 layer which has surface hoar to size 20 mm. Not a problem today with no slab above, but is now perfectly protected by the 5-10 cm that overlies the layer. Watch out for this one starting next storm.

reports.title: Bow Summit Study Plot - Snow Profile
reports.comment: snowpack: Easy failures on the December 15 surface hoar in this snow profile, but limited slab development above this layer. In general the snowpack is becoming weaker as it facets but it is still supportive to skiers in most areas. Lots of recent loose dry sluffing observed out of steep gullies in the area.

reports.title: Cirque Forepeak
reports.comment: avalanche: I triggered a very small slide in a small bowl on Cirque Forepeak. We were still on the approach and had to descend the bowl and climb the other side to reach our objective. The descent and ascent were maybe 20 m. I made the mistake of heading straight across an untouched slope while still in tour mode (splitboard) and the fresh snow crumbled and slid immediately. This is fairly protect…

reports.title: Crowfoot Glades
reports.comment: quick: Didn't notice any problems.  The skin track it pretty packed down and slick...could have used some ski crampons.

reports.title: auto: Quick Report
reports.comment: quick: Skied West Nile area today, and found good skiing. Snowpack is heavily faceted. Did not come across any major windslab development. Snowing lightly throughout the day with 3-4cms falling while we were skiing.

reports.title: Bow Summit
reports.comment:
quick: Observed a recent rider triggered size 1.5 in the alpine. Triggered on convex rocky NE facing ~40° slope with thinner snowpack and likely wind affected. Guessing a 30 - 40 cm crown about 5 - 10m wide and ran for about 30 - 50m.

About 40 cm of kind of well consolidated snow on about 100 cm of loose facets at treeline.

reports.title: Observation Sub Peak
reports.comment: quick: Skied and boot packed up the south ridge of Observation Sub Peak and down the glacier on the North side and back out the col between Observation Sub Peak and Cirque Peak.  We did not see any evidence of recent natural slab activity.  We did note sloughing from steep north facing terrain that appeared several days old and some significant snowballing on steep solar aspects especially near ro…

reports.title: Conditions: Observations Sub Peak
reports.comment:
quick: Glacier Travel on North Side:
extremely variable coverage with 15cm to 300cm on snow depth. Be wary

Solar aspects:

Got cooked

Windward Sloped:
Wind scoured sloped evident from the road, 15cm-100cm left depending on aspect. Thick windslab on Northerly aspects. SW sloped pretty beat up. / weather: Getting pretty warm out there

reports.title: The nile
reports.comment:
quick: Couple laps on the fan NE/E. Decent riding, mostly surface facets on decently supportive crust.  Found some consolidating surface snow on solar aspects. -7 at car high of -2
No cloud, no wind until the afternoon 
Noted surface hoar 5-10mm as low as 2000m
Dug a quick pit on NE aspect 2060 

Cth 27 d80cm on fc 2-4mm
Ctm 15 d12cm on sh 5-10mm
Cth 26 d80cm on fc 2-4mm

reports.title: Crystal Ridge
reports.comment: quick: Poked around a bit at treeline on Crystal Ridge. The alpine looked pretty wind hammered so we decided to stay in sheltered zones in the trees.  Pretty consistent temps all day but at mid-day the winds shifted from SW light to SE-E moderate with strong gusts and light snow.  Dug a quick pit around 2400m, SW aspect.  Height of snow 120cm with the upper half composed of a complex mix of sun/te…

reports.title: West Nile
reports.comment: quick: Good skiing BLT - 20+cm of fresh snow covering the old tracks. Saw 1 size 2.5 soft slab from the upper cliffs which ran down to the bench adjacent to the moraine features at treeline. Also a couple of size 2.0 slabs out of the Noseum paths facing the highway.

reports.title: auto: Quick Report
reports.comment: quick: Went up to Helen Shoulder, wrapped around and set a skin track up the mellow South and east facing slopes rather than the burn. Great riding in the Glades and lower angle slopes, lots of shooting cracks and whumphing below treeline while putting in the skin track.

reports.title: Wedge / Mosquito
reports.comment: quick: Went for a walk in the trees up towards Wedge ok above the mosquito drainage.  Temps -12 to a mid-day high around -8, winds nil to light SW.  Very light snow (ice fog crystals) all day with 1cm accum.  Limited visibility due to ice fog and occasional valley cloud.  Observed no new, natural avy activity but there are large east facing cornices off the south ridge of Dolomite that look prime.…

reports.title: Parks Canada - Bow Summit Study Plot profile
reports.comment: snowpack: We are still getting Moderate to Hard sudden shears on the weak December 15 facet interface which is down 60cm.  If the storm snow above this layer is triggered, it will be easy for avalanches to step down to this interface resulting in large avalanches.

reports.title: Observation Subpeak
reports.comment:
quick: There was good fresh snow to be found on mellow slopes. We avoided anything steep or exposed to overhead hazard. 

The three big persistent layers were obvious in the rutschblock we dug. It failed at R6 on the December 15 layer.

reports.title: Cirque Forepeak
reports.comment:
quick: Spooky travel on Cirque Forepeak today. Many whumphs observed across the benches. Remote triggered a size 1 from across a gully feature around 100m away. Crown looked to be between 0.5-1m deep on approx 30 degree slope on a NW aspect. Decent skiing. 

Evidence of fresh slides size 1-2 on N/NW aspects observed in the afternoon.

reports.title: Bow Summit
reports.comment: quick: Widespread wind effect all aspects TL & ALP. Fresh (12-24hrs), natural avalanche cycle to size 3.5 observed along highway 93 N corridor, suspect failure on January's persistent weak layers which were found down 65-80cm in test pits at Bow Summit: CTE-M down 65 and 75 on Jan 15 & Jan 6 SH/FC, HS 170cm. Snowpack is complex, and the lower snowpack continues to facet with cold temperatures. Goo…

reports.title: Crowfoot Glades
reports.comment: quick: No results on ECT. HS 200 cm. East aspect. -20C at 1PM. 5mm wind slab starting to form above treeline.

reports.title: Peyto-Bow
reports.comment: quick: A week late but since we haven't had another major weather event, I believe conditions are probably still similar. Went into Peyto hut on Sat. Feb.17th with the traditional double creek crossing. Stayed on the treed bench to access the moraine and final 50m required ski crampons. The lower glacier has glacier depth poles which can help in poor visibility. Cold and Windy on Sun. Feb.18th. On…

reports.title: Peyto Hut - slope by moraine
reports.comment: avalanche: Sa, large 1 or small 2. Hard wind slab running on facets, crown 20cm - 40cm, ran 100m +. One person involved, no injury, no lost equipment, stayed on top of the hard slab. Photo is from a phone - triggered up and left of top red mark, by rock, and stopped below the lower red mark. Slide is obvious if you're skiing up to the hut - its the slope next to the boot pack going up the moraine

reports.title: Bow Summit Snow Profile
reports.comment: quick: Results from the Parks Canada - Bow Summit study plot

reports.title: Helen Shoulder
reports.comment: quick: Good conditions at Helen Shoulder. Observed small cracks on isolated windslabs at 2250m (near ridge top) on South aspect. Good stability otherwise.

reports.title: Cirque Forepeak
reports.comment: quick: Variable conditions in the alpine with lots of wind affect.  Wind loaded pockets presenting wumphs and cracks.  Triggered size 1.5 hard slab likely on a sun crust on the south facing slope at the summit of cirque forepeak.  Pit results on SE slope showed 8 cm recent snow, 20 cm old storm layer, then consolidated down 1m.  CTM 24 failing in the middle of the consolidated layer 50-60 cm down …

reports.title: bow summit size 2 2018-03-09
reports.comment: quick: We triggered size 2 300m slope at Bow Summit @ ~12:30pm. We had done 1 lap of the lower 100m slope before gaining the higher 300 m slope. We Noted that the slope curvature and wind were different above, but should have taken this more into consideration. After finishing the skin up to 300 m gain, we skied 1 at a time down. While parts of the slope skier's left were similar to the lower sect…

reports.title: COTR AST 2: Helen Shoulder
reports.comment: weather: Humidity Levels (RH) were increasing through the day. Moderate ridge top winds. / snowpack: New storm interface not bonding well to melt freeze crust. Crust not supportive up to 2200m. On north aspects we had no failures with our compression tests. On south aspects 20cm down SC (drop) below crust in facets. R-Block 1.

reports.title: Cirque peak
reports.comment: quick: Went up the Helen creek to Helen lake and Cirque peak. Dropped down the North couloir (read rappelled down). And skied back to the road via the drainage NW of Cirque Peak. The trip in to Helen lake we noted one east facing slope with storm slabs forming up. A few small cracks. We had one wumph on a south east low angle slope near the lake.  Heading up Cirque peak the snowpack is thin but we…

reports.title: Surprise sunny day, good snow up top
reports.comment: quick: The snow in the alpine was holding out pretty well with the warm weather.  Bottom of the valley was pretty sticky.

reports.title: Skiier Accidental - Observation Subpeak
reports.comment: avalanche: Report from public who triggered avalanche. 1 skiier went for a 200m ride and lost gear but ended up on surface and was uninjured. The party was able to self evacuate. The bed surface was likely a suncrust.

reports.title: Mt. Gordon (Wapta)
reports.comment:
quick: Ascended Mt. Gordon from Bow Lake today. We had low visibility and at times white-out conditions with brief clear periods. Snow above the canyon was crusty, but softened on the headwall below the hut. 
Great powder above the hut, made for an awesome ski down from Gordon.

reports.title: Flower Couloir/Bow Summit
reports.comment: quick: Crossed an older size 2 slab debris pile on east aspect around 2350m. Saw multiple older point release size 1.5 near exposed rock on very steep east aspects at around 2600m. Ski cut two size 0.5 soft slabs at around 2750m and 2500m on N/NE aspects.

reports.title: Crowfoot Pass
reports.comment: quick: Lot's of fresh avalanche activity off the east face of Crowfoot Mountain and skier's right side of the descent gully from the Pass. Ranging from size 2.0 to 2.5 - storm snow slabs stepping down in places. Lot's of wind transport happening up high. Good skiing in the trees - 25 to 30 cm ski pen.

reports.title: Crowfoot Trees
reports.comment: quick: Great day skiing the mellow slopes at crowfoot trees. Observed a size 2 mid afternoon that buried fresh ski tracks in the lower portion of the gully to skiers far left. Was not there in the morning. Likely triggered from debris off the cliffs above. See attached pics

reports.title: Cirque Peak North couloir
reports.comment: quick: Went up Cirque Peak today and dropped into the North couloir. Significant and bone chilling wumpfing on SE aspect in the cirque bowl as we come up from Num Ti Jah. Traverse was low angle so didn’t pose huge problems. You can skin up except for last 120m before switching to bootpacking. North couloir requires a 30m rap and some additional down climbing before hitting decent snow. Snow was he…

reports.title: Jimmy Simpson Junior
reports.comment: quick: Wet surface snow in low angle lower elevations.  Wind pressed, but not slabbed snow on the alpine slopes.  Skied a SE to E aspect run.  Dug do look for the Mar 15th PWL but found no evidence of it.  Snow was well consolidated in the column and right side up (fist for first 20, 4F for next 20cm, 1F for the balance of column (pit was 1m deep).  No failure in a column test.  Column was dug jus…

reports.title: Laps at Crowfoot Gladed
reports.comment: quick: Got into the crowfoot glades around 10am and rode them until 4pm. Sun was out in our area most of the day and packed a punch (we definitely over dressed). Temperature was +6 at the top of tree line with the diffused sun. Snow started off light and fluffy and quickly became heavy just an hour or so in. At the end of the day when the sun was completely gone a crust started to freeze up. Loose…

reports.title: Flower Couloir, Bow Summit
reports.comment: quick: Snowpack felt stable and good. Stickier on alpine sun aspects but good and soft on north aspects and treeline. One very localised whump on top of a roller / mound with some small exposed rocks - assumed rocks underneath and exposed area with recent snowfall and wind affect the cause, no other signs of instability. / avalanche: Skier triggered size 1-2 avalanche in the Flower Couloir about 4…

reports.title: Crowfoot Couloir avalanche
reports.comment: quick: Three of us left our vehicle around 7:30 to ski the Crowfoot Couolir. Condtions were beautiful, broken clouds and the sunrise poking through, temps just below freezing. We skinned the apron and transitioned to boot packing at base of couloir, arriving at top just around 8:45. Snow in couloir was powder mixed with some debris from sluffs from the previous days. We saw no major snow movement …

reports.title: Crowfoot Galdes
reports.comment: quick: Roughly 5 of New snow today while skiing Crowfoot Glades. Temps -2 at TL at 1:30, with light SW winds.  We stayed away from solar slopes and skied steep N to NE facing terrain at TL. We skier triggered two to three size 0.5 wind slabs. They were 10-15cm down and formed an obvious slab which propagated roughly 5m. They ran up to 10m. They were on NE facing terrain at 2100m. They were trigger…

reports.title: Awesome and stable ski conditions
reports.comment: quick: Excellent skiing with limited visibility.  Fresh tracks for everyone. -4C at 8:30am to -2C at 1pm. Snowing consistently and heavily. Cross-loading observed in the alpine so we stayed below treeline.

reports.title: Mosquito Creek Glades
reports.comment: quick: 20-30 cm of storm snow over the last 48 hours was beginning to consolidate into a slab at the tree line. This layer is sitting on a hard crust about 5 cm thick and slid under our skis on a couple occasions, but didn’t propogate. We chose our terrain carefully and skied below the treeline. The new spring snow made for a nice descent despite the underlying crust, although it was getting wet w…

reports.title: Skier accidental
reports.comment: avalanche: Skier accidental, no involvement.

reports.title: Cirque peak
reports.comment: quick: Trip to Cirque peak from winter trailhead, down Nbowl and out the drainage btw Cirque and Observation sub-peak. -9 at 6:30 and rock hard snow. Almost needed ski crampons going up the luge run. There were signs of activity on solar aspects from steep rocky terrain (mostly sloughing) & one size 2.5 off one of the Dolomite gully. Travel was good with close to 0 ski penetration. We ski crampone…
